vision: A standalone, headless Decimal calculation engine for leveraged crypto trading — salvaged from the retired TradingDashboard app so the rebuild depends on it instead of reimplementing leverage, DCA, and hedging math.

calc_primitives.description: New pure-Decimal calc primitives the TradingDashboard rebuild's future roadmap needs — hedging engine, per-account/concentration metrics, options + margin-bridge math, funding math. Each is a delta_calc module the dashboard's future tasks consume instead of reimplementing.

calculators.description: Port the pure risk/hedging calculators out of the retired TradingDashboard app into DeltaCalc.*

consumer_math.description: Pure-Decimal decision/aggregation primitives the dashboard touches on every screen — PnL/breakeven, net-delta hedging, portfolio-margin liquidation, stress scenarios, fees, funding carry. Value-in/value-out over inputs the consumer already holds (own state + exchange-supplied mark price, funding rate, option deltas). No option pricing — Greeks/IV come from the exchange (Deribit); a Black-Scholes lib is a separate later concern, explicitly out of scope here.

v0_1.description: Proves the salvaged calculators run standalone (no Phoenix/Ecto/I-O) with their original test suites green, so the TradingDashboard rebuild can depend on DeltaCalc instead of reimplementing the math.

v0_3.name: Consumer decision primitives
v0_3.description: The math the dashboard reaches for at the call-site: position PnL/ROE/breakeven net of fees+funding, net-delta rebalancing from exchange-supplied option deltas, portfolio-margin liquidation across netted positions, price-shock stress scenarios, fee modeling, and funding carry/break-even. Consumer-driven (delta_calc IS the consumer's math layer). Option pricing stays out — exchange supplies Greeks/IV; BS is a future separate lib.

task.title: Fix Funding.compare_funding_rates cross-cadence ranking: max/min and arbitrage from raw rates, annualized at per-venue cadence

task.body:
Audit-surfaced bug (Codex second-opinion, audit pass on 0da3fcf..HEAD; see .audit/bb6175c.md).

`DeltaCalc.Funding.compare_single_symbol/2` selects `max_exchange`/`min_exchange`, `delta`, and the `arbitrage_opportunity` flag from RAW per-period funding rates, but `annual_apr_delta/5` then annualizes each venue at its OWN cadence (`periods_per_day_for(venue)`) and subtracts. When venues have different cadences (the `%{venue => periods}` form introduced by task 28), the annualized spread can come out NEGATIVE and the venue labels invert.

Specific trigger:
  Funding.compare_funding_rates(
    %{hourly: Decimal.new("0.0001"), eight_hour: Decimal.new("0.0007")},
    %{hourly: 24, eight_hour: 3}
  )
ranks :eight_hour as max by raw rate (0.0007 > 0.0001), then annual_apr_delta = (0.0007*3*365*100) - (0.0001*24*365*100) = 76.65 - 87.60 = -10.95 — even though the hourly venue has the HIGHER annualized rate (87.60% vs 76.65%). max_exchange/min_exchange are mislabeled and the APR delta is negative/nonsensical.

The deeper question is a domain decision: `@arbitrage_threshold 0.0005` is a raw per-period value with no defined meaning across cadences. Decide whether cross-cadence ranking + arbitrage detection should operate on annualized (or per-day-normalized) rates throughout, and what the threshold becomes in those units. Same-cadence (scalar periods_per_day) behavior must stay unchanged — raw and annualized ranking agree when the cadence is constant, so only the mixed-cadence path changes.

Add a property/unit test for the mixed-cadence ranking inversion so coverage no longer ratifies the bug.

task.body:
`Funding.compare_funding_rates/2` now returns a `:delta` whose unit depends on the SHAPE of the `periods_per_day` argument: a scalar cadence yields a raw per-period spread (e.g. `0.002`), while a `%{venue => periods}` map yields a per-day-normalized spread (e.g. `0.0003`). This is documented in the `@doc` and intentional, but it leaks into `find_arbitrage_opportunities/2`, whose default `min_delta` (`0.001`) was tuned for the raw per-period scale. Mixed-cadence comparison maps are filtered against a threshold ~3x too large, so genuine daily-normalized spreads can be silently dropped, and a caller cannot mix scalar- and map-derived comparison results in one `find_arbitrage_opportunities` call without scale skew.

Decide the domain-correct contract: either (a) make `:delta` a single consistent unit across both paths and adjust `annual_apr_delta` accordingly, or (b) keep dual units but make `find_arbitrage_opportunities` cadence-aware (normalize its `min_delta`, or read a unit tag off the comparison entry). task.title: Fix inverted min_delta raw→daily scaling in Funding.find_arbitrage_opportunities (divide vs multiply)
acceptance_criteria: find_arbitrage_opportunities raw→daily min_delta scaling matches the file's own arbitrage-threshold convention (raw threshold × periods_per_day to reach daily terms), or a documented justification is given for why min_delta diverges
A raw per-period spread strictly below min_delta is excluded after daily normalization; one at/above is included — proven by a worked dimensional example in the test, not re-asserting current output
The task-36 golden test 'normalizes min_delta for venue-cadence-map comparison entries' is re-derived from first principles, not from the inverted scaling
:raw_per_period (scalar-cadence) filtering behavior is unchanged

Remove the `@tag :domain_pending` from the task-37 raw→daily scaling test in test/delta_calc/domain_invariants_test.exs so the invariant runs green under mix ci
out_of_scope: Changing the arbitrage threshold domain constant (@arbitrage_threshold) itself
Changing the :delta unit tagging contract introduced by task 36
task.body:
Task 36 added `threshold_for_delta_unit/2` so `find_arbitrage_opportunities/2` filters `:daily_normalized` comparison entries against a cadence-aware threshold. The scaling DIRECTION appears inverted. For `:daily_normalized` entries it computes `min_delta / @default_periods_per_day` (divide by 3), but the daily delta is `raw_rate * periods_per_day` — LARGER than a raw per-period spread, not smaller. To express a raw per-period `min_delta` on the same daily basis as the delta it is compared against, it should be MULTIPLIED by periods, not divided.

The decisive internal evidence: the SAME daily code path normalizes its arbitrage gate raw→daily by MULTIPLYING — `@mixed_cadence_arbitrage_threshold = @arbitrage_threshold * @default_periods_per_day` (0.0005 * 3 = 0.0015), with a docstring that explicitly calls this "the default 8-hour raw threshold normalized to daily terms". So the file uses ×periods for one raw→daily conversion (arbitrage threshold) and ÷periods for the other (min_delta) — contradictory directions for the identical conversion. Consequence: daily-normalized entries pass `min_delta` filtering ~9x more permissively than intended, the opposite of "filter scalar- and map-cadence results together without scale skew".

Root cause to watch for: task 36's own body framed the original bug as "filtered against a threshold ~3x too large, so genuine daily-normalized spreads can be silently dropped" and illustrated the map delta as `0.0003` (smaller than raw) — both dimensionally backwards, since daily = raw × periods is larger. The implementer faithfully encoded the backwards premise, and the golden test (`normalizes min_delta for venue-cadence-map comparison entries`, min_delta 0.0045 → threshold 0.0015) was computed WITH the inverted scaling, so coverage ratifies it. Re-derive the threshold from dimensional analysis, not from the existing golden.

Verify against the daily path's arbitrage threshold convention and a worked example: a raw per-period spread below `min_delta` must NOT pass once normalized to daily, and one at/above must. Pure Decimal, no I/O. Scalar-cadence (`:raw_per_period`) filtering must remain unchanged.

task.title: Standardize funding-rate unit (fraction) across all DeltaCalc modules
acceptance_criteria: Every funding-rate :value parameter across the library uses ONE documented unit (fraction, e.g. 0.0001 = 0.01%)
MarginBridge and OptionsRisk no longer divide funding inputs by 100; their docs/examples updated to the fraction convention
A caller can feed the same funding-rate value to Hedging.calculate_funding_cost AND MarginBridge.stress_test_prolonged_negative and get dimensionally consistent results
A manifest/consistency test (or doctest) pins the unit convention so drift fails CI
mix ci clean; money-math modules stay >= 95% coverage
Remove the `@tag :domain_pending` from the task-38 funding-unit test in test/delta_calc/domain_invariants_test.exs so the invariant runs green under mix ci
task.body:
The library uses two incompatible funding-rate units. Funding.*, Carry.funding_yield, and Hedging.calculate_funding_cost/3 treat the rate as a FRACTION (0.0001 = 0.01%, no /100). MarginBridge.stress_test_prolonged_negative / check_kill_switch and OptionsRisk (which delegates to MarginBridge) treat it as a PERCENT number and divide by 100 internally. A consumer who derives one funding rate and passes it to both a Hedging function and a MarginBridge function is off by 100x, silently.

Pick the fraction convention (it matches Funding, the canonical funding module) and make every funding-rate input across the surface use it: update MarginBridge's internal /100, its api() descriptions and examples, and OptionsRisk's pass-through. This is a cross-module domain invariant that no per-task reviewer caught because each module is internally consistent — encode the chosen unit in a consistency test so it can't drift again.

task.title: Unify Decimal coercion into one module with a single fail-loud error policy
acceptance_criteria: A single coercion helper (e.g. DeltaCalc.Decimal.coerce/1) replaces the ~13 per-module to_decimal/ensure_decimal/cast_rate copies
Funding.ensure_decimal no longer silently returns 0 on unparseable input — invalid input fails loudly or returns a tagged error consistent with the rest of the module
One documented policy for invalid input (raise vs tagged error) applied uniformly; the ex_dna disable comments for the duplicated clauses are removed
A decision is recorded on whether public money/price/leverage APIs accept raw floats; if rejected, affected tests are updated
mix ci clean (ex_dna --max-clones 0 passes without the per-module disables)
out_of_scope: Changing the public return shapes of calc functions
Reworking the funding-rate unit convention (separate task)
task.body:
Decimal coercion is reimplemented in ~13 modules with three divergent error policies: explicit clauses with no fallback (Calc -> FunctionClauseError on nil), Decimal.cast + {:ok,_}= match (PnL/Fees/etc -> MatchError), and silent-zero (Funding.ensure_decimal returns Decimal.new(0) on garbage, which then ranks as a venue's funding rate and corrupts comparison/arbitrage output). Two modules carry # ex_dna:disable-for-lines to suppress the clone detector.

Extract one coercion module with a single, documented failure contract and delete the copies. Decide and document whether public money/price/leverage inputs should accept raw floats at all (current code admits binary-float artifacts via Decimal.from_float/cast, and tests lock that in) — if you tighten it, update those tests. The silent-zero path is the priority: a money library must not fabricate 0 from bad input.

task.title: Manifest consistency test must cover unannotated public functions
acceptance_criteria: ManifestConsistencyTest asserts every public function in a registered module is advertised via api() (compare __info__(:functions) against __api__(), excluding generated/callback functions)
DCAPlanner.calculate_dca_ladder/10 is either annotated with api() or made private/deprecated so it is no longer an unadvertised public function
The new check fails CI when a public function lacks api()
mix ci clean
task.body:
All three ManifestConsistencyTest invariants iterate mod.__api__() — the ADVERTISED surface — never mod.__info__(:functions). So a public function with no api() annotation is invisible to every check: it is not tested for uniqueness, registration, or :hints. DCAPlanner.calculate_dca_ladder/10 is exactly such an escaped public function.

Add an invariant that compares each registered module's actual public functions against its advertised api() set, so an unannotated public function fails CI. Then resolve calculate_dca_ladder/10 (annotate or privatize). This closes the whole-surface blind spot the manifest test exists to cover.

acceptance_criteria: Calc.dca_ladder MMR re-tiering no longer hardcodes notional thresholds (50k/250k/1M) and multipliers; the tier schedule is caller-supplied or the tiering is removed from the generic engine

Tests cover a non-default tier schedule and a non-8h cadence

Replace the task-41 `flunk` placeholder and remove its `@tag :domain_pending` in test/delta_calc/domain_invariants_test.exs (caller-supplied tier schedule changes the liquidation result) so the invariant runs green under mix ci

Generic calc functions bake in venue/risk-engine constants. Calc.calculate_tiered_mmr hardcodes a tier ladder (0-50k base, 50k-250k x1.5, 250k-1M x2, 1M+ x2.5) inside the DCA liquidation path; MarginBridge's kill-switch thresholds assume an 8h/default cadence while sibling functions accept periods_per_day. Make the tier schedule and cadence caller-supplied :value inputs (or drop tiering from the generic engine entirely). Any default left in place must be documented as a convention and be overridable, with a test proving a non-default value flows through.

Short DCA callers therefore cannot get correct side-aware averages or liquidation through the public surface. task.title: Fix PortfolioMargin netted mark price for offsetting legs
acceptance_criteria: Net exposure no longer uses a single gross-quantity-weighted mark across offsetting long/short legs when those legs have different marks
Maintenance margin and liquidation price are correct for a book with offsetting legs at different mark prices (worked example in test)
Behavior for a single-instrument, single-mark book is unchanged
mix ci clean; PortfolioMargin coverage >= 95%
out_of_scope: Changing the netting model for same-mark books
task.body: PortfolioMargin.net_exposure collapses the book to one gross-quantity-weighted average mark price, then applies it to the NET quantity for maintenance margin and liquidation. For offsetting legs marked at different prices, that blended mark is not the net position's mark, so combined_maintenance_margin and portfolio_liquidation_price are wrong. Group by instrument (or compute signed notional over net quantity, or require identical marks per netted exposure) so the netted-book math is correct when longs and shorts are marked differently. Prove it with a worked offsetting-legs example, and keep single-mark books unchanged.

task.title: Resolve ignored/dead public parameters and add entry-price guards
acceptance_criteria: Each currently-ignored public parameter is either wired into the calculation or removed from the public signature AND its Descripex metadata: Calc.dca_ladder mark_buffer, Calc.calculate_dca_price side, PositionCalculator fee_rate and mode_config
PositionCalculator position sizing guards against zero/negative entry_price (tagged error or documented sentinel) with a test
No public function advertises a parameter it ignores
mix ci clean
task.body:
Several public functions accept parameters they silently ignore, making the advertised contract lie. Calc.dca_ladder documents mark_buffer but binds it as _mark_buffer and never applies it. Calc.calculate_dca_price takes _side but multiplies regardless, so short ladders depend entirely on caller-signed multipliers with no guard. PositionCalculator.calculate_position accepts fee_rate (never folded into mmr_total) and mode_config (fetched but unused in sizing — only echoed in output). PositionCalculator also divides by entry_price with no zero/negative guard.

For each ignored parameter: either wire it into the math (e.g. fold fee_rate into the liquidation MMR buffer; let side drive dca price direction; apply mark_buffer to the MMR/liquidation calc) or remove it from the public signature and Descripex metadata. Add a zero/negative entry_price guard with a test.

task.title: Unify output-precision and rounding policy across modules
acceptance_criteria: A documented rounding policy states the output precision per value domain (price, rate, percentage, ratio)
Module rounding (Calc.quantize 8 places; Funding 6/4/2; Hedging 2/4/8) either follows the documented policy or each deviation has a stated rationale
The decimal 3.x precision-34 implications (per CLAUDE.md) are accounted for at output boundaries

task.body: There is no single output-precision policy. Calc.quantize rounds to 8 places, Funding rounds to 6/4/2 depending on field, Hedging rounds 2/4/8 ad hoc, PortfolioMargin reuses Calc.quantize. Given the documented decimal 3.x default-precision change (28 -> 34), inconsistent boundary rounding across modules is a real correctness surface, not just style. Define a per-domain rounding policy (price vs rate vs percentage vs ratio), apply it consistently, and document any intentional per-field deviation.
